messages:
mike: quick heads-up — ran a targeted perf run on paged-attn + several FlashAttention variants. saw intermittent GPU stall spikes that line up with batched IO completions when multiple short-seq requests are inflight. not a steady regression but spikes cause 99p latency to jump ~3x for affected routes.

jasleen: can you paste the perf snippet / repro steps? is this only with paged KV or also dense KV?

mike: repro: load generator hitting chat-route with seq lengths ~40, concurrency 120, batching window 6ms, KV hit rate ~68%. toggling paged-kv on/off reproduces spike. attached lightweight logs:

```
# nvprof summary (trimmed)
Kernel: flash_attn_fwd_v2  time: 2.1ms  occupancy: 70%  stall_mem: 18%  stall_pipe: 6%
Kernel: paged_kv_merge    time: 0.9ms  occupancy: 55%  stall_mem: 46%  stall_pipe: 12%
GPU activity timeline: [—active—][IO-complete pause(1.2ms)][—active—]
Observed 99p latency jumps from 28ms -> 92ms during pause windows
```

omar: interesting — stall_mem for paged_kv_merge is the red flag. sounds like when multiple page faults resolve and we drain IO completions on the host, the kernel backpressure causes warps to idle. are we coalescing multiple IO completions on the host thread and then invoking a big memcpy+kernel?

ciara: that matches my earlier theory about inflight IO coalescing creating micro-bursts. we currently batch page-fetch completions into a single callback to reduce interrupts. but that creates a short period of high DMA work then a tight sequence of kernel launches. worth trying: 1) spread completions across event loop ticks, or 2) do small prefetch of likely hot pages so coalescence magnitude drops.

ryan: quick test patch: changed pager to stagger completion callbacks by up to 0.5ms (jitter). simple node:

```
// pseudo
on_io_complete(batch) {
  for (i, p : enumerate(batch)) {
    schedule_work( p, delay = i * jitter_ms );
  }
}
```

Result: 99p latency drops to ~36ms in local run, GPU stall_mem for paged_kv_merge drops ~60% -> 28%. Not perfect but big improvement.

jasleen: nice. any kernel selection interaction? maybe flash_attn variant switching under high-latency NVLink paths?

mike: good point — we have dynamic kernel selector that chooses fused vs tiled variants based on sequence len distribution and measured kernel throughput. during these bursts selector sometimes flips to a variant with worse memory usage which exacerbates stall. need to make selector aware of transient IO backpressure signals (e.g., queued_io_depth).

omar: agreed — we should add a simple cost term: expected_io_backpressure * mem_bandwidth_penalty to discourage variants with heavier mem transfer during high queued_io. trivial heuristic: if queued_io_depth > X then avoid mem-heavy kernel unless it gives huge compute win.

ciara: also check batching heuristic. our 6ms window is tuned for throughput but for short seq chat workloads it packs too many small requests and increases page contention. maybe use adaptive batching: target tokens-per-batch and max inflight-pages threshold.

mike: notes for follow-up ACTIONs: 
- add jittered completion option as an opt-in flag (ryan already has patch)
- expose queued_io_depth to kernel selector as signal (omar + jasleen)
- add prefetch heuristics for hot prefixes to reduce page-miss bursts (ciara)
- run full canary on dedicated pool tonight, measure 99p and stall metrics (mike/ryan)

deploy-bot: deploy queued: pager/jittered-completion @staging scheduled in 10m. CI: green. :rocket:

ryan: attaching quick flame summary (text):
```
Flame root: request-loop
  - batching (35%)
  - flash_attn_fwd_v2 (22%)
  - paged_kv_merge (18%)  <-- memory stalls concentrated here
  - memcpy (10%)
  - scheduler (5%)
```

mike: thanks. i'll run the canary and post metrics. if staging looks good we can enable opt-in flag for a subset of customers. short takeaway: inflight IO coalescing helps CPU/interrupt overhead but can create GPU-memory microbursts that trip kernel mem stalls; solutions: jitter completions, make kernel selector IO-aware, and limit batch sizes by pages-in-flight.

ciara: sounds good. pls add the new perf counters to the console: paged_kv_io_depth and paged_kv_stall_mem_pct so we can alert when this regresses.

jasleen: i'll file a tiny RFC for selector-weight change and add the perf graphs dashboard ticket.

mike: closing loop once canary finishes. thanks all :thumbsup:
